description:
Move acquire, renew, heartbeat, force-evict and lease listing onto the held lease lock, so no operation repeats the lock and publish steps by hand.

## Background

Each lease operation in `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs` hand-rolls its lock, load, evict, append and write steps (`acquire_claim_synchronized` `:659`, `heartbeat` `:824`, `renew_lease` `:1016`, `force_evict_lease` `:1142`, `get_active_leases` `:1188`). Two paths evict an expired lease in memory and then fail without writing the index, so the eviction is dropped and logged again by the next reader: `renew_lease` evicts at `:1024-1025` and then returns `LeaseNotFound` (`:1028-1034`) or the not-owner error (`:1037-1046`); the acquire path does the same in `acquire_claim_with_reason`, which evicts at `:556-558` and bails at `:568`, `:584` and `:599` before its index write at `:636`; that method is test-only and is deleted before this change, but the production acquire must not reintroduce its drop when it moves onto `apply`. `acquire_claim_synchronized` writes the index right after evicting (`:712-713`), so its later failures at `:738`, `:751` and `:763` keep the eviction; a failure of its repository synchronization (`:799`) happens after the lease write. `evict_expired_at` appends the eviction record to `claims.jsonl` before removing the lease from the in-memory index (`:911-921`), so what a failing renew drops is only the index write, which the lock-free `read_leases` returns. The indefinite-lease limits count every lease (`:744-771`). `ClaimCoordinator::lock()` returns a `LeaseLock` with `load`, `list` and `apply`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Acquire, renew, heartbeat, force-evict and lease listing each take one `LeaseLock` and change leases only through `apply`. Acquire checks the indefinite-lease limits through `list()` and runs its repository synchronization while holding the lock.
- [hard] REQ-02: Renew, heartbeat and force-evict, still addressed by lease id, find the lease through `list()`; this is `lease-id-scan-bridge`, an interim lookup whose removal is issue addressing.
- [hard] REQ-03: When a renew or an acquire evicts an expired lease and then fails, the eviction stays persisted in the store `apply` publishes. Regression tests cover a renew that fails as not found or not owned, and an acquire that fails after evicting. After each failure, a lock-free `read_leases` no longer returns the evicted lease, and after a later listing through the lease lock the claims log still holds exactly one eviction record for it.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Lease operations run through the lease lock
